title: AI made my dream game possible: I'm building a full MMORPG on my own, and the closed beta starts November 25
author: Imelda-Online
selftext:
For as long as I can remember I wanted to make my own MMORPG. The old-school kind: big packs of monsters, loot that changes how your hero looks, upgrading your weapon to +10 and praying it doesn't fail, building a guild with your friends and fighting the guild war on Sunday night. But an MMO is a game studio's job. Code, art, 3D models, animations, servers, a website... for one person it was never realistic.



AI changed that. Over the last 4 months I built \*\*Imelda Online\*\*, a free action MMORPG that runs in your browser, on PC and phone, no download. And on November 25 it goes into closed beta.



**What's in it right now**

\- 5 classes (Warden, Sage, Hunter, Shadow, Shaman) with 91 skills

\- Pull whole packs of monsters and burn them down with area skills

\- Armor sets that change your look, gear upgrades up to +10, Runes and reforging

\- 7 towns, player stalls for trading, 15 mounts, wings and companions

\- Parties, 7 dungeons, 147 kinds of monsters and 27 bosses

\- Guilds: found one with your friends, guild chat, War Tribute from hunting strong monsters

\- Duels, arena 1v1 / 2v2 / 5v5, a 10v10 Battleground, and every Sunday the Guild War: guilds fight for 5 flags, and the winner rules the Moonlands for a week

\- The Moonlands (PvPvE from level 100), 10 rebirths, and the Sun Rift as the endgame



**How AI made it possible**

**Code:** I build the game together with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code). I decide what the game should be and how it should feel; the AI helps me write and fix the code, from the combat to the multiplayer server. I test everything myself and keep steering.

**Art:** I run image models locally on my own PC (ComfyUI). I trained a LoRA on my own style so every monster, hero and item looks like it belongs in the same world. I pick and reject a lot: the style only stays consistent because I'm strict about it.

**3D:** The characters start as 2D designs, get turned into 3D models (image-to-3D), are rigged and animated, and then rendered in the game.

**Everything around it:** the website, the trailers and even the sign-up mails were made the same way.



AI didn't make the game for me. It's more like having a team that works as hard as I do, while every decision about the game is still mine. For me, it's the difference between "one day maybe" and an actual beta date.



**Closed beta: November 25**

Sign up at: [https://imelda-online.com/](https://imelda-online.com/)   
On November 25 everyone on the list gets a login by email. It's free to play, and supporting is only cosmetic.

I'd love to hear what you think, and I'm happy to answer anything about the workflow: the LoRA, the 3D pipeline, working with an AI coder on a project this size.
